title.en: Yuki-Onna: The Woman of the Snow

author.zh: 小泉八云（拉夫卡迪奥·赫恩）

edition.en: From Kwaidan: Stories and Studies of Strange Things (Boston and New York: Houghton, Mifflin, 1904), as transcribed by Project Gutenberg (eBook 1210), checked against a scan of the 1904 edition: the transcriber’s bracketed notes, a picture caption and an added “a” (“a situation as servant”) are removed. Hearn’s two short footnotes, on the two-mat hut and on the name O-Yuki, are given as glosses.
edition.zh: 出自《怪谈：奇异事物的故事与研究》（波士顿与纽约：霍顿·米夫林出版社，1904），据古登堡计划电子书第 1210 号，并以 1904 年版扫描本校核：删去录入者加的括号注释、一处插图说明和多出来的一个“a”（“a situation as servant”）。赫恩关于两叠小屋和“阿雪”这个名字的两条简短脚注，改作注释。

basis.en: Published in 1904; Lafcadio Hearn died in 1904.
basis.zh: 1904 年出版；小泉八云卒于 1904 年。

note.en: Hearn, born in Greece to an Irish father, settled in Japan, took the name Koizumi Yakumo and spent his last years retelling Japanese tales in English; he says this one was told to him by a farmer of Chōfu, near Tokyo. It is a winter story of a promise made in a snowstorm and kept for years, until it is broken by lamplight over the sewing. It belongs beside Andersen’s Snow Queen, and like it, it is told plainly enough for a child.
note.zh: 赫恩生于希腊，父亲是爱尔兰人，后来定居日本，改名小泉八云，晚年用英语重述日本的故事；他说这一篇是东京附近调布的一位农民讲给他听的。这是一个冬天的故事：一个在暴风雪中许下的诺言，守了许多年，直到在做针线的灯光下被打破。它可以和安徒生的《冰雪女王》放在一起，也像那篇一样，讲得简单到孩子也能听懂。

excerpt.orig: Even as she screamed, her voice became thin, like a crying of wind;—then she melted into a bright white mist that spired to the roof-beams, and shuddered away through the smoke-hole.
excerpt.en: Even as she screamed, her voice became thin, like a crying of wind;—then she melted into a bright white mist that spired to the roof-beams, and shuddered away through the smoke-hole.
excerpt.zh: 就在她尖叫的时候，她的声音变细了，像风的呜咽；接着她化成一团明亮的白雾，盘旋着升到屋梁，颤抖着从烟孔里飘散了……

gloss.en: The old province that took in most of present-day Tokyo and parts of Saitama and Kanagawa.
gloss.zh: 武藏国，旧时的令制国，大致包括今天的东京都以及埼玉、神奈川两县的一部分。

gloss.en: Hearn’s note: a hut with a floor of about six feet square, two tatami mats.
gloss.zh: 赫恩原注：地面约六英尺见方的小屋，即两张榻榻米大小。

gloss.en: Mino, cloaks of straw or sedge worn by farmers and woodcutters against rain and snow.
gloss.zh: 蓑衣，用稻草或莎草编成，农夫和樵夫用来遮雨挡雪。

gloss.en: A junk is a flat-bottomed Chinese or Japanese sailing ship.
gloss.zh: junk，中国或日本的平底帆船。

gloss.en: Snow-light: the faint glow that snow gives off in the dark.
gloss.zh: 雪明かり，雪光：黑暗中积雪发出的微光。

gloss.en: Yedo, or Edo, the old name of Tokyo.
O is an honorific prefix. Hearn’s own note says the name, which means Snow, is not uncommon.
gloss.zh: “阿”（お）是表示亲切或尊敬的前缀。赫恩原注说，这个名字意为“雪”，并不少见。

gloss.at: Ki ga aréba, mé mo kuchi hodo ni mono wo iu
gloss.en: Hearn translates the proverb in the next words.
gloss.zh: 日语谚语“気があれば目も口ほどに物を言う”，赫恩随即把它译了出来。

gloss.at: the light of a paper lamp
gloss.en: An andon: a lamp with a paper shade around an oil wick, the usual light of a Japanese house.
gloss.zh: 行灯，用纸糊灯罩围住油灯芯，是日本旧式人家常用的灯。

gloss.en: Yuki-onna, a spirit of snowstorms in the folklore of northern and mountain Japan.
gloss.zh: 雪女，日本北部和山区民间传说中暴风雪的精灵。

gloss.en: The opening in the roof of a farmhouse through which the smoke of the hearth escaped.
gloss.zh: 农舍屋顶上排出炉烟的孔。

note.en: A plainly told winter legend of a promise kept for years and broken by lamplight; Hearn’s telling is the best known, though it is a retelling, not an invention.
note.zh: 平实讲述的雪夜传说，誓约守了多年，终在灯下破了；小泉八云的版本最为人知，但属重述而非独创。
